title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
claim: A single attached oxygen atom does not account for the two magnetic behaviors of rare-earth clusters: above about 200 K, Tb_n and Tb_nO generally have the same deflection behavior, with only specific low-temperature exceptions.
explanation: Because terbium is monoisotopic, Tb_n and Tb_nO are resolved for n < 40. Above 200 K the clean and oxygenated clusters match. At the lowest temperatures, Tb21O and Tb25O deflect less than locked Tb21 and Tb25 and resemble the intermediate regime, consistent with oxygen helping to unlock the moment at a lower temperature. Conversely, Tb22 remains predominantly superparamagnetic at all temperatures, while Tb22O is partially locked at low temperature and becomes predominantly superparamagnetic when hot.
scope: Terbium clusters with one oxygen atom, n < 40, compared with the corresponding clean clusters.
conditions: Low-temperature differences are reported for Tb21O and Tb25O; Tb21 and Tb21O match by 198 K, and Tb25 and Tb25O match above 248 K. Fig. 3 fields are 0.267 T at 98 K, 0.405 T at 148 K, and 0.540 T at 198 K.
caveats: The authors' statement that oxygen has little effect is explicitly qualified by these low-temperature exceptions. The unlocking and partial-locking roles of oxygen are size specific and not a general oxygen effect.
